title: Manipulation of Single Neural Stem Cells and Neurons in Brain Slices using Robotic Microinjection
protocol: Prepare 3% agarose by separately dissolving 3 g of wide range agarose and 3 g low-melting point agarose in 100 mL of cell culture-grade PBS in two separate 200 mL glass bottles, respectively.
Store prepared agarose at room temperature for up to 3 months.
Dissolve 1 g of sodium bicarbonate and Tyrode’s salt in 1 L of distilled water.
Adjust the pH of the solution to 7.4.
Filter the Tyrode solution through a 0.2 µm bottle-top filter.
Add 10 mL of rat serum to Neurobasal medium.
Add 1 mL of 2 mM glutamine to the mixture.
Add 1 mL of penicillin-streptomycin (100x) to the mixture.
Add 1 mL of N-2 supplement (100x) to the mixture.
Add 2 mL of B27 supplement (50x) to the mixture.
Add 1 mL of HEPES buffer (pH 7.3) to complete the Slice Culture Medium (SCM).
Aliquot 5 mL of SCM into 15 mL tubes.
Store aliquoted SCM at -20 °C.
Dissolve powder in 200 mL of distilled water to prepare 5x DMEM modified low-glucose solution without phenol red.
Filter the 5x DMEM solution through a 0.2 µm bottle-top filter.
Mix 20 mL of filtered 5x DMEM solution with HEPES buffer, N2 supplement (100x), B27 supplement (50x), penicillin-streptomycin (100x), and 2 mM glutamine to prepare CIMM.
Add 74 mL of distilled water to the mixture to make a total volume of 100 mL for CIMM.
Store prepared CIMM at 4 °C.
Dissolve 262 mM NaHCO3, 0.05 N NaOH, and 200 mM HEPES in distilled water to prepare reconstitution buffer.
Sterilize the reconstitution buffer by filtration through a bottle-top 0.22 µm filter system into a sterile glass bottle.
Aliquot 500 µL of sterilized reconstitution buffer into airtight microcentrifuge tubes.
Store aliquoted reconstitution buffer at 4 °C.
Dissolve fluorescently labeled Dextran in RNase free distilled water to prepare the microinjection dye stock with a final concentration of 10 µg/µL.
Prepare 5 µL aliquots of the microinjection dye stock.
Store prepared dye aliquots at -20 °C until use.
Pull microinjection pipettes from borosilicate glass capillaries using the micropipette puller.
Protect the pulled pipettes from dust.
Do not store pipettes for more than 2 – 3 days.
Melt the 3% wide range agarose using a microwave oven prior to brain tissue dissection.
Keep the melted agarose in a water bath at 37 °C until needed.
Thaw an aliquot of SCM and warm 10 – 12 mL CIMM to 37 °C using a water bath.
Warm 20 mL of Tyrode’s solution to 37 °C using a water bath.
Mix the fluorescent tracer with the other chemical(s) to be injected to final concentration 5 – 10 μg/μL.
Centrifuge the microinjection solution at 16, 000 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant and transfer into a new tube.
Keep the microinjection solution on ice until use.
Use the heads from E13.5 – E16.5 mouse embryos to prepare organotypic tissue slices of the telencephalon.
Remove the skin and open the skull using forceps, moving along the midline.
Dissect out the embryonic brain from the open skull and remove the meninges covering the brain tissue starting from the ventral side of the brain.
Leave the dissected whole brain in Tyrode’s solution on a 37 °C heating block.
Pour wide range melted agarose into a disposable embedding mold.
Transfer the brains (maximum of 4) into the cooled agarose using a Pasteur pipette.
Stir the agarose around the tissue without touching it, using a spatula or Dumont #1 forceps.
Let the agarose solidify at room temperature.
Trim excess agarose surrounding the tissue once solidified.
Fill the buffer tray with PBS.
Orient the brain with the rostro-caudal axis perpendicular to the tray (use olfactory bulbs as landmark).
Cut 250 µm slices using a vibratome.
Fill a 3.5 cm Petri dish with 2 mL of prewarmed media.
Transfer slices (10 - 15) using a plastic Pasteur pipette into the Petri dish containing prewarmed media.
Shift the Petri dish with slices into the slice culture incubator.
Maintain slices at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 40% O2 / 5% CO2 / 55% N2 until use.
Turn on the computer, microscope, microscope camera, manipulators, pressure rig, and pressure sensor.
Load the application by clicking the file “launchapp.py” in the main folder downloaded from GitHub and specify the device settings.
Create an outward pressure to prevent unwanted clogging before submerging the pipette into the solution.
Slide the compensation pressure bar to 24 – 45% and click Set Values.
Tune the pressure to a sufficient pressure by turning the mechanical pressure valve knob to 1 – 2 PSI (69 – 138 mbar) as indicated by the pressure sensor.
Transfer slices to be microinjected into a 3.5 cm Petri dish containing 2 mL of pre-warmed CIMM.
Place the Petri dish with slices to be microinjected in the centre on the preheated (37 °C) microinjection stage.
Load the microinjection pipette with 1.4 –1.6 μL of microinjected solution using a long-tip plastic pipette.
Insert the microinjection pipette onto the pipette holder.
Bring the slice into focus using the lowest magnification on the microscope.
Guide the micropipette to the field of view (FOV) so that it is focused on the same plane as the slice target.
Switch the output of the microscope to the camera to see the FOV in the application.
Click the magnification button in the top left of the interface to initiate device calibration.
Select the 10x magnification or whatever magnification the lens is set to and press OK.
Refocus the pipette tip using the micrometric wheel of the microscope.
Click the pipette tip with the cursor.
Press the step 1.1 button and press OK in the popup window.
The pipette will move in the Y direction.
Click the tip of the pipette and press the step 1.2 button.
Enter 45 into the Pipette angle box and press the Set angle.
Enter desired parameters into the Automated microinjection controls panel.
Set injection distance to 20 – 40 µm for apical progenitors.
Set depth to 10 – 15 µm for apical progenitors.
Set injection distance to 30 – 40 µm from the basal side for neurons.
Set depth to 10 – 30 µm depending upon what is being targeted for neurons.
Always set speed to 100%.
Click Set values.
Draw edge button and drag cursor along desired trajectory in popup window.
For microinjecting progenitor stem cells, target ventral side of the telencephalon surface.
Bring pipette to start of line and click tip of pipette.
Click Run trajectory to start microinjecting.
Repeat step for every plane of injection targeted (usually done for 3 – 4 planes with 40 – 75 injections per plane).
Prepare collagen mixture (1.5 mg/mL): Add 1.25 mL matrix solution, 0.5 mL distilled water, 0.5 mL 5x DMEM-F12 solution and 0.25 mL reconstitution buffer to a tube.
Keep the mixture on ice until use.
Obtain the Petri dish containing the microinjected slices from the slice culture incubation chamber.
Immerse the slices into the collagen mixture.
Transfer 200 – 300 µL of collagen mixture with the slices into a 14 mm well of a 35 mm glass-bottom dish.
Ensure that the slices are covered in very little collagen.
Orient the slices using two pairs of forceps, ensuring there is enough space between them.
Incubate the Petri dish for 5 min at 37 °C on a heating block to allow collagen to solidify.
Move the Petri dish back to the slice culture incubator for an additional 40 min.
Add 2 mL of prewarmed SCM to the slices after 40 min.
Keep the slices in culture until the desired time point.
Take the slices out of the slice culture incubator and aspirate the SCM.
Wash the collagen-embedded slices with 1x PBS.
Add 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (in 120 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.4).
Leave the tissue at room temperature for 30 min.
Move the tissue to 4 °C for overnight fixation.
Aspirate the paraformaldehyde solution the next day.
Perform 1x PBS washes on the fixed slices.
Use two pairs of forceps to gently extract the slices under a stereomicroscope.
Use a microwave to melt 3% (wt/vol) low melting point agarose.
Pour the melted agarose into a disposable embedding mold and let it cool to around 38 – 39 °C.
Transfer tissue slices from step 5.7 into the mold containing cooled agarose using a plastic Pasteur pipette.
Ensure that the pial side of the slice is up and the ventricular surface faces down.
Let the agarose cool down to room temperature to solidify.
Trim the extra agarose surrounding the slices.
Orient the agarose block to ensure that the cut surface is parallel to the vibratome’s cutting blade.
Using a vibratome, cut 50 µm thick sections.
Fill a 24 well dish with 1x PBS.
Transfer the sections into this dish using a fine-tip paintbrush.
Perform immunofluorescence as per standard protocols.
